propositions: Requiring literal canonical section headings rejects valid plans where executable content is carried by semantic aliases or compact checklist form
Placeholder-detection lexicon produces false positives on mechanically decidable bounded conditionals; phrase presence alone does not indicate deferred design
Strict per-AC proof-marker detection rejects precise behavioral oracles lacking explicit `verified by` sentinels
Edit-set requirements are inapplicable to read-only analysis and external-attestation work with explicit no-edit output contracts
Deterministic AC conjunction counting cannot distinguish bundled independent deliverables from atomic cross-surface matrices
Testing section negative-scenario requirements produce false positives on mechanical/non-user-facing work where failure taxonomies are inapplicable
